decision.reason: Official filing alone is sufficient for a bounded materiality assessment; supplementary research is unavailable and not required to summarize the disclosed spouse transactions and uncertainty.

implications: Watch later filings for repeated additions to tax-advantaged short-duration or municipal fixed-income vehicles; repetition would strengthen a defensive or liquidity-parking interpretation.

Watch whether the many small equity sales and scattered equity buys resolve into a clearer sector rotation in later disclosures; this filing alone shows repositioning, not a single high-conviction stock call.
Because these were disclosed as the spouse's transactions and reported after the fact, any signal is conditional and should not be read as the member's current holdings, timing, or intent.
brief.interpretation: The filing shows the spouse, not the member, making a high-volume February 2026 portfolio rebalance. The clearest disclosed pattern is multiple large purchases in Northern Tax-Advantaged Ultra-Short Fixed Income and Northern Intermediate Tax Exempt Fund, alongside municipal-bond, private-fund, REIT, healthcare, industrial, and technology trades, while many other equity and municipal positions were sold. That is potentially useful as a tentative household risk-positioning signal toward tax-advantaged cash or short-duration income, but the disclosure is delayed, lacks exact values, includes duplicate rows, and does not establish current holdings or intent.

materialFacts.statement: Filed March 10, 2026, the PTR reports spouse transactions notified March 5, 2026, with trade dates concentrated in February 2026.

The filing lists numerous separate spouse purchases of Northern Tax-Advantaged Ultra-Short Fixed Income on Feb. 11, 2026, with disclosed amount bands from $15,001-$50,000 up to one line labeled 'Spouse/DC Asset Over $1,000,000'; duplicate rows are present and the filing does not give exact totals.

The filing also lists numerous spouse purchases of Northern Intermediate Tax Exempt Fund on Feb. 11, 2026, plus another purchase on Feb. 19, 2026, including one line labeled 'Spouse/DC Asset Over $1,000,000' and multiple additional lines from $15,001-$50,000 to $500,001-$1,000,000.

Other disclosed spouse purchases include Hawaii ST GO BDS and Phoenix Ariz Civic Impt Corp Wtr Sys at $100,001-$250,000 each, Baxter International and Healthpeak Properties at $100,001-$250,000 each, and private-fund interests such as Mays-Allocate 2025 LP and HPS Special Opp Fund II LP.

The sales side includes Kentucky St Ppty & Bldgs Commn Revs Bds at $250,001-$500,000; Donaldson Company, Eagle Mtn & Saginaw Tex Indpt Sch Dist, Dallas Tex Indpt Sch, and Alexandria Real Estate Equities at $100,001-$250,000; and separate Kane Cnty Ill Cmnty Unit Sch Dist and Woodridge Ill GO Ref sales at $50,001-$100,000 each.

sources.label: Signed House periodic transaction report for Michael T. McCaul
sources.publisher: Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives

brief.title: Spouse disclosed broad February rebalance with very large Northern fund purchases and offsetting sales
uncertainty: The filing provides only amount ranges, not exact dollars, and an 'Over $1,000,000' label does not disclose an upper bound.
Several Northern fund entries are duplicated, so the filing supports repeated transactions but not a precise aggregate commitment from this evidence alone.
No tickers or verified security mappings are provided here, and delayed disclosure does not establish current holdings, motive, or performance.

unknowns: Exact aggregate size of the duplicated Northern fund purchases.
Whether the LP entries were subscriptions or capital calls rather than open-market transactions.
Whether any sold positions were fully exited or only trimmed.
